**Precondition:** A consumer may be held liable only if the institution provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1)-(3). If an access device was involved, it must be an accepted access device and the institution must have provided a means to identify the consumer [R-1005.6#1].

- The creditor may not make or threaten an adverse credit report, or report delinquency, because you didn't pay the disputed amount [R-1026.13#2].

Separately, 1026.12(c) lets a cardholder withhold payment up to the amount outstanding for property or services in a dispute with the merchant. This applies only if the cardholder made a good-faith attempt to resolve the dispute, and it carries an amount and location limitation, with listed exclusions [R-1026.12#2].

Short answer: 1026.13 does not let you stop paying the entire bill. It lets you withhold only the disputed portion.

It also may not accelerate your debt or restrict or close your account solely because you exercised these rights in good faith [R-1026.13#2].

If the creditor later determines you owe some or all of the amount, you get time to pay it, and the creditor may report delinquency only after that period [R-1026.13#3].
